entities.summary:
The Battle of Lugdunum, fought on February 18, 197, was a pivotal event in the Roman Empire's struggle for power. This decisive battle pitted the forces of Septimius Severus against those of Clodius Albinus, two powerful Roman generals vying for control. The conflict took place in Lugdunum, the capital of the Roman province of Gaul, and marked a turning point in the history of the empire.

 The battle was a brutal and bloody affair, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. Septimius Severus emerged victorious, but his triumph came at a great cost. The Roman Empire would never be the same, as the power struggles that began at Lugdunum would continue to shape the course of Roman history for generations to come.

 The Battle of Lugdunum had far-reaching consequences, as it paved the way for the rise of the Severan dynasty and set in motion the events that would lead to the final decline of the Roman Empire. As the centuries passed, the legacy of Lugdunum would be felt in the tumultuous history of the Roman world. 

 In the end, the Battle of Lugdunum stands as a testament to the brutal and unforgiving nature of power politics, a reminder that even the greatest empires are built on the backs of blood and steel.
